title: Slice-sheaf coinduction for internal group restriction
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ and a $\mathcal V$-small site $(C,J)$ with finite limits [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Put $\mathscr E=\operatorname{Sh}(C,J)$. For a sheaf of groups $K$ with $\mathcal V$-small values, let $\mathscr E^K$ be the category of sheaves of sets $X$ with a natural left action $K\times X\to X$ satisfying the identity and associativity laws; its maps are equivariant sheaf maps. Let $L$ be another sheaf of groups and $\theta:L\to K$ a morphism, and let $\operatorname{Res}_\theta:\mathscr E^K\to\mathscr E^L$ replace $k\cdot x$ by $l\cdot x=\theta(l)\cdot x$. For $Y\in\mathscr E^L$, define $B_\theta(Y)(U)$ to be the set of natural maps of sheaves $F:K|_U\to Y|_U$ on $C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] such that $F_V(\theta(l)k)=l\cdot F_V(k)$ for every $V\to U$, $l\in L(V)$, $k\in K(V)$. Restriction is relocalization of these maps. These sets are $\mathcal V$-small and form a sheaf. The formula $(a\cdot F)_V(k)=F_V(k\,a|_V)$ defines a natural left $K$-action on it. Postcomposition with an $L$-equivariant map makes $B_\theta:\mathscr E^L\to\mathscr E^K$ a functor. There is an adjunction $\operatorname{Res}_\theta\dashv B_\theta$ with the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_L(\operatorname{Res}_\theta X,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_K(X,B_\theta Y)$ given by $\widehat u_U(x)_V(k)=u_V(k\cdot x|_V)$ and inverse $v\mapsto(x\mapsto v_U(x)_U(1))$. The two displayed maps are inverse on every test object and natural in both variables. No injectivity or surjectivity hypothesis on $\theta$ is imposed.

proof.text: For each $U$, the objects $(V\to U)$ and arrows of $C/U$ form $\mathcal V$-small sets. The underlying set of natural maps $K|_U\to Y|_U$ is a subset of $\prod_{(V\to U)}\operatorname{Map}(K(V),Y(V))$, hence is $\mathcal V$-small by the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Imposing the displayed equivariance equations gives another subset. Relocalization [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] sends such a map to its restriction on $C/V$; the same equations still hold there. Restricting twice is restricting along the composite, sectionwise, and restriction along an identity changes nothing. Thus the prescribed sets and restrictions form a small-valued presheaf.

proof.text: Let $\{U_i\to U\}$ be a covering and let $F_i\in B_\theta(Y)(U_i)$ agree on double fibre products. Apply the morphism-gluing clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] to $P=K|_U$ and $Q=Y|_U$, using relocalization [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] to identify their restrictions with $K|_{U_i}$ and $Y|_{U_i}$. This gives a unique sheaf map $F:K|_U\to Y|_U$ with those restrictions. The hypotheses of that clause hold: $C$ is small with all fibre products, and the family and section values lie in the stipulated universe. This invocation uses only the morphism clause, not effective descent of objects.

proof.text: The glued map lies in $B_\theta(Y)(U)$. For $V\to U$, $l\in L(V)$ and $k\in K(V)$, restrict $F_V(\theta(l)k)$ and $l\cdot F_V(k)$ to the covering $\{V\times_U U_i\to V\}$. Naturality of $F$, $\theta$ and the action identifies these restrictions with the equal expressions for $F_i$. Separatedness of the sheaf $Y$, namely uniqueness of amalgamation in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], makes the two sections equal. Uniqueness of $F$ as a map also gives uniqueness in $B_\theta(Y)(U)$. This proves the sheaf condition, including an empty covering.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written internal-action categorical infrastructure; explicit expansion of former steps 4–6 of lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction, preserved in its Q21 report.

proof.text: For $a\in K(U)$ define $(a\cdot F)_V(k)=F_V(k a|_V)$. For $h:W\to V$ over $U$, restriction of this value is $F_W(k|_W a|_W)$, so this is a natural slice map. Its equivariance is $(a\cdot F)_V(\theta(l)k)=F_V(\theta(l)(k a|_V))=l\cdot F_V(k a|_V)$. Restriction along $U'\to U$ commutes with this construction, so the operation is a sheaf map $K\times B_\theta(Y)\to B_\theta(Y)$. The identity acts trivially, and $(a\cdot(b\cdot F))_V(k)=F_V((k a|_V)b|_V)=F_V(k(ab)|_V)=((ab)\cdot F)_V(k)$; these are the left-action laws.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written internal-action categorical infrastructure; explicit expansion of former steps 4–6 of lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction, preserved in its Q21 report.

proof.text: For an $L$-equivariant sheaf map $b:Y\to Y'$, put $B_\theta(b)_U(F)=b|_U\circ F$. Naturality of $b$ makes this commute with relocalization. Its defining equation is $b_V(F_V(\theta(l)k))=b_V(l\cdot F_V(k))=l\cdot b_V(F_V(k))$, and $B_\theta(b)(a\cdot F)(k)=b(F(k a))=(a\cdot B_\theta(b)(F))(k)$. Thus it is a $K$-equivariant sheaf map. Postcomposition with an identity is the identity, and postcomposition with $b'b$ is consecutive postcomposition with $b$ and $b'$. Together with the previous steps this constructs the functor $B_\theta$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written internal-action categorical infrastructure; explicit expansion of former steps 4–6 of lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction, preserved in its Q21 report.

proof.text: Given $u:\operatorname{Res}_\theta X\to Y$, set $\widehat u_U(x)_V(k)=u_V(k\cdot x|_V)$. For $h:W\to V$ over $U$, naturality of $u$ and the action gives $u_V(k\cdot x|_V)|_W=u_W(k|_W\cdot x|_W)$; hence this is a natural slice map. It is $L$-equivariant since $u_V((\theta(l)k)\cdot x|_V)=u_V(\theta(l)\cdot(k\cdot x|_V))=l\cdot u_V(k\cdot x|_V)$. Replacing $U$ by $U'\to U$ in the formula proves naturality of $\widehat u$ as a sheaf map. Finally $\widehat u_U(a\cdot x)_V(k)=u_V((k a|_V)\cdot x|_V)=(a\cdot\widehat u_U(x))_V(k)$, so it is a $K$-map.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written internal-action categorical infrastructure; explicit expansion of former steps 4–6 of lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction, preserved in its Q21 report.

proof.text: Given a $K$-map $v:X\to B_\theta(Y)$, set $u_U(x)=v_U(x)_U(1_U)$. For $h:V\to U$, naturality of the slice map $v_U(x)$ and then of $v$ gives $u_U(x)|_V=v_U(x)_V(1_V)=v_V(x|_V)_V(1_V)=u_V(x|_V)$, so $u$ is a sheaf map. Its $L$-equivariance is $u_U(\theta(l)\cdot x)=(\theta(l)\cdot v_U(x))_U(1_U)=v_U(x)_U(\theta(l))=l\cdot v_U(x)_U(1_U)$, the last equality using the defining equation for $v_U(x)$ at $k=1_U$. Thus $u:\operatorname{Res}_\theta X\to Y$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written internal-action categorical infrastructure; explicit expansion of former steps 4–6 of lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction, preserved in its Q21 report.

proof.text: Starting with $u$, evaluation of $\widehat u_U(x)$ at $1_U$ gives $u_U(1_U\cdot x)=u_U(x)$. Starting with $v$, the reconstructed map has at $(U,x;V\to U,k)$ the value $v_V(k\cdot x|_V)_V(1_V)=(k\cdot v_V(x|_V))_V(1_V)=v_U(x)_V(k)$, by $K$-equivariance and naturality of $v$. Thus the constructions are inverse on every test object. For a $K$-map $f:X'\to X$, equivariance gives $\widehat{u\circ\operatorname{Res}_\theta(f)}(x')(k)=u(k\cdot f(x'))=u(f(k\cdot x'))=(\widehat u\circ f)(x')(k)$. For an $L$-map $b:Y\to Y'$, $\widehat{b\circ u}(x)(k)=b(u(k\cdot x))=(B_\theta(b)\circ\widehat u)(x)(k)$. These are exactly both naturality laws for the Hom bijection.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written internal-action categorical infrastructure; explicit expansion of former steps 4–6 of lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction, preserved in its Q21 report.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] with $F=\operatorname{Res}_\theta$, $G=B_\theta$ and the bijections of steps 6–8. Its hypotheses are precisely the functoriality proved above and the two displayed naturality identities. This produces $\operatorname{Res}_\theta\dashv B_\theta$ with the stipulated Hom bijection and inverse. All equations used only that $\theta$ is a group-sheaf homomorphism; no injectivity or surjectivity has been used.

(7) u=v(-)(1) is L-equivariant via (θ(l)·G)(1)=G(θ(l)). (8) Both composites are the identity, using v_V(k·x|_V)(1)=(k·v_V(x|_V))(1)=v_U(x)_V(k), and both naturality laws hold.
